content:
The test image shows soybean stems that remain **green** while the pods have matured and turned brown/golden. No leaves are visible (dropped), but stems are clearly still green. This pattern strongly suggests **Green_stem_disorder** or possibly **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus** (which can also cause green stems after pod maturity).

Let me check reference images for both candidates and a few others.

The Green_stem_disorder reference is a near-perfect match — top-right panel shows green stems with mature brown pods, identical to the test image. Bean_Pod_Mottle shows leaf mottling/mosaic and dark seeds, not present here.

Let me view more reference images to meet the minimum requirement.

All evidence points clearly to **Green_stem_disorder**:

- **Test image**: Green stems with fully mature, brown/golden pods hanging on them; no leaves present (dropped); surrounding plant material is dry/dead
- **Green_stem_disorder reference** (top-right panel): near-identical — green stem + mature brown pods, same background of dry crop debris
- **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus**: would show leaf mottling/mosaic, dark seeds — not present
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: shows interveinal chlorosis/necrosis on leaves, rotted roots — not seen
- All other candidates (Diaporthe, Anthracnose, White_Mold, rust, etc.) show completely different symptom patterns

The defining feature — stems remaining green while pods have fully matured — perfectly matches Green_stem_disorder's description: *"stems stay moist and green while pods may mature normally."*
